01 · Instruction Fine-Tuning

Follow the instruction, don't just continue the text

A base model is trained to predict the next token, so it tends to continue the pattern. Instruction tuning teaches it to treat a prompt as a request. Flip the switch and watch the same prompt get two very different answers.

Base model vs instruction-tuned

Pick a prompt, then toggle the model.

Base model

Base model — continues the pattern

Build a training example

Instruction tuning is supervised learning on examples shaped like this. Edit the fields and copy the formatted example.

Thousands of diverse examples like this — not just more of one task — is what teaches a model to follow unseen instructions.

02 · RLHF

Learn a reward from your preferences, then optimize against it

Humans find it easier to say "this one's better" than to score answers out of ten. Rank the responses below and a toy reward model learns what you like. Then use the KL slider to see the reward-hacking trade-off from the deck.

Train a toy reward model

Reorder these four answers to a support question, best at the top. The model learns weights over four features and predicts a reward.

Rank the answers, then teach the model. It nudges its weights toward the features your top picks share.

The KL leash

In PPO the model maximizes reward − β·KL(policy ‖ reference). Slide β and watch the trade-off.

0 — chase reward hard1 — barely move
